conclusion: This single-case pilot supports Bateia as a source-discovery and evidence-packaging aid; it did surface different leads, but does not establish superior overall insight quality or reduced total human/assistant work.

bateia_assisted: bounded one-hop expansion from project collections

direct: official algorithm/API material and research papers
bateia: automatic catalog dispatch and README collection
off-domain engineering leads from communities and museum software

weaknesses_observed: 4 of 6 selected references provided insufficient returned material for the proposed insights
all 20 logical calls were spent on DIRECT (11) and BROADENED (9); ALTERNATIVES/TRADEOFFS/COUNTEREXAMPLES had no executed cell
selected reading cards mainly contain introductions; deeper workflow evidence required reading full returned README
timeouts/auth/integrity failures reduced coverage; do not call those sources irrelevant
next_improvement_priorities: schedule calls to cover both perspectives and suitable source types under the global budget
include an explicit applicability/relevance reason before consuming a reference slot
recognize collection/index READMEs and propose bounded reference follow-up with provenance
select passages describing workflow/constraints, not only matching introductory words
experimental_limits: one problem, same assistant and non-blind analysis
asymmetric channels: adaptive web versus fixed catalog policies; raw request counts not comparable costs
anonymous run, missing AtomGit token and several provider timeouts
no user validation or code changes; all five proposals are hypotheses
